mainTopic: The אורים ותומים: how they answer and who may ask; the opening of פרק יום הכפורים and the law of חצי שיעור
overview: This amud finishes the ברייתא about consulting the אורים ותומים. דוד asked out of order and was answered in order, and two questions may be asked together only in an emergency. A decree of the אורים ותומים is never reversed, and its name means its answers are clear and always come true. The גמרא defends this rule using the war at גבעת בנימין. It then records how the letters on the חושן gave the answer, either by standing out (רבי יוחנן) or by joining together (ריש לקיש). The names of the אבות and the words שבטי ישורון were added so that the whole alphabet was present. A worthy כהן with רוח הקודש was also needed, and only national leaders could ask, as רבי אבהו learns from a פסוק. After the הדרן, פרק יום הכפורים opens with the five עינויים and the amounts for eating and drinking. The גמרא explains why the משנה says 'אסור', using the מחלוקת about חצי שיעור, and begins a challenge from oaths that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: דוד asked out of order but was answered in order
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its point: דוד asked his two questions in the wrong order, and the אורים ותומים answered in the right order.
steps.simpleTranslation: [דוד asked] out of order, and they answered him in order.
steps.whatsHappening: The sentence began on the previous page. The ברייתא is describing how דוד asked the אורים ותומים two questions in the wrong sequence, and the answer followed the correct sequence instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד asked, 'Will the people of קעילה hand me over? Will שאול come down?' Logically, שאול must come down before anyone can hand דוד over to him. So the answer addressed שאול's coming first: 'He will come down.' The אורים ותומים answered according to the proper order, not the order of the question.

keyTerms.meaning: They answered him (literally: returned to him)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The subject is דוד, who was asking about קעילה and שאול in שמואל א׳ פרק כ״ג. The rule just before this was that you normally ask only one thing at a time.

phrases.english: [He asked] out of order,
phrases.notes: He asked about קעילה before asking about שאול's coming

phrases.english: and they answered him in order.
phrases.notes: The answer 'He will come down' answered the question that logically comes first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's description of David's question from the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When questions are asked out of order, the אורים ותומים answer in the correct logical order.

steps.title: דוד realized his mistake and asked again in order
steps.stepSummary: Once דוד saw he had asked out of order, he asked his second question properly. A פסוק proves this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And once he realized that he had asked out of order, he went back and asked in order, as it says: 'Will the men of קעילה hand me and my men over to שאול? And ה׳ said: They will hand you over.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows that דוד corrected himself. After learning that שאול would come, he asked separately whether the people of קעילה would hand him over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is that the פסוק repeats only the קעילה question, as its own question. This shows דוד asked it again as a single question in the right order, and it received its own answer, 'They will hand you over.'

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and asked again

phrases.english: And once he realized that he had asked out of order,
he went back and asked in order,
as it is stated: 'Will the men of Keilah hand over
phrases.notes: שמואל א׳ כ״ג:י״ב

phrases.english: me and my men into the hand of Saul?
And God said: They will hand [you] over.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁשָּׁאַל שֶׁלֹּא כַּסֵּדֶר, חָזַר וְשָׁאַל כַּסֵּדֶר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened to the second question that was not answered the first time
steps.raayaObject: That only one question is answered at a time, so the second question had to be asked again in order

steps.title: Exception: an urgent matter allows two questions at once
steps.stepSummary: If the situation requires two answers at once, both are answered. The proof is דוד's pursuit of the raiders of צקלג.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the matter needs two [answers], they answer him two, as it says: 'דוד asked ה׳, saying: Shall I pursue this troop? Will I overtake them? And He said to him: Pursue, for you will surely overtake and surely rescue.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds an exception to the one-question rule. When there is a real need for two answers together, such as an emergency, both questions are answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד asked two questions: 'Should I chase them?' and 'Will I catch them?' He got a full answer to both, and even extra information, 'you will rescue.' Because the situation was urgent, there was no time to ask one at a time.

phrases.english: But if the matter required two —
phrases.notes: An urgent situation needing two answers at once

phrases.english: they answer him two,
as it is stated: 'And David asked of God, saying:
phrases.notes: שמואל א׳ ל׳:ח׳

phrases.english: Shall I pursue this troop? Will I overtake them?
And He said to him: Pursue,
for you will surely overtake and surely rescue.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הוּצְרַךְ הַדָּבָר לִשְׁנַיִם — מַחְזִירִין לוֹ שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exception to the one-question-at-a-time rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When there is a real need, two questions may be asked together and both are answered.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the ordering rule is a standard procedure that bends when necessity demands it.

steps.title: A decree of the אורים ותומים is never reversed
steps.stepSummary: A נביא's negative decree can be cancelled, but a decree of the אורים ותומים is final. The source is the phrase 'במשפט האורים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though a נביא's decree can be reversed, a decree of the אורים ותומים cannot be reversed, as it says: 'By the judgment of the אורים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא compares the reliability of a נביא with that of the אורים ותומים. It rules that the answer of the אורים ותומים always comes true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נביא's bad prophecy can be reversed, for example through תשובה, as happened with יונה and נינוה. The אורים ותומים are called a 'משפט', a judgment, and a court's final ruling stands. So their decree cannot change.

keyTerms.meaning: By the judgment of the אורים (במדבר כ״ז:כ״א)

steps.whatToRemember: A נביא's decree can be undone. A decree of the אורים ותומים always stands, because it is called a 'משפט', a final ruling.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגְּזֵירַת נָבִיא חוֹזֶרֶת —
phrases.english: And even though a prophet's decree can be reversed —
a decree of the Urim VeTummim is not reversed,
as it is stated: 'By the judgment of the Urim.'
phrases.notes: במדבר כ״ז:כ״א. A judgment is final.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגְּזֵירַת נָבִיא חוֹזֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how to ask to how reliable the answer is
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A decree of the אורים ותומים is never reversed, unlike a decree of a נביא.

steps.title: Why are they called אורים ותומים?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the meaning behind the name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are they called אורים ותומים?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The ברייתא asks about the meaning of the name and is preparing to explain it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question about the name, not an attack on anything. The answer will connect the name to the qualities just discussed: clear answers that always come true.

keyTerms.meaning: The oracle placed in the כהן גדול's breastplate
Why are they called by this name?

phrases.english: Why is their name called Urim VeTummim?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to explaining the name
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the names אורים and תומים mean

steps.title: אורים make their words clear; תומים make them come true
steps.stepSummary: אורים comes from 'אור', light, because they make their words clear. תומים comes from 'תם', complete, because their words are always fulfilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'אורים' because they light up their words. 'תומים' because they complete their words.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by explaining each half of the name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אורים means their answers are clear, lit up like light. תומים means their answers are 'completed', meaning they always come true. This matches the earlier rule that their decree is never reversed.
steps.whatToRemember: אורים means clear answers, and תומים means answers that always come true.

phrases.english: 'Urim' — because they illuminate their words,
phrases.notes: From אור, light

phrases.english: 'Tummim' — because they fulfill their words.
phrases.notes: From תם, complete

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the name
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אורים because they make their words clear. תומים because their words are always fulfilled.

steps.title: Challenge from the war at גבעת בנימין
steps.stepSummary: If the אורים ותומים always come true, why did the people lose at גבעת בנימין after being told to go to war?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: at גבעת בנימין, why did the answers of the אורים ותומים not come true?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a challenge against what it just said, that the words of the אורים ותומים are always fulfilled. It points to a story where that seems to have failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ספר שופטים, the people asked the אורים ותומים three times about fighting שבט בנימין, and each time they were told to go up. They lost the first two battles. That seems to contradict the claim that תומים means its words always come true.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible objection)
גבעת בנימין, site of the civil war against שבט בנימין

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier נביא rule. The challenge here is not about a decree being cancelled. It is about an answer that seemed simply wrong.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
At Gibeah of Benjamin,
why did they (the Urim VeTummim) not come true?
phrases.notes: Refers to the first two battles in שופטים כ, which were lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תֹּאמַר: בְּגִבְעַת בִּנְיָמִין מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא הִשְׁלִימוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 6's claim that תומים means their words are always fulfilled.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the words of the אורים ותומים are always fulfilled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: At גבעת בנימין they were told to fight but lost twice, so the answer seems not to have come true.

steps.title: They never asked whether they would win
steps.stepSummary: The first two times they did not ask about victory. When they finally asked, the answer agreed and they won.
steps.simpleTranslation: They had not asked whether they would win or lose. At the end, when they did ask, the answer agreed with them, and it came true.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge. The אורים ותומים never promised victory in the first two battles, because nobody asked about victory.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier questions were only about whether to go and who should lead. They were not about the outcome. So losing did not make any answer false. The one time they asked about winning, they were told yes, and they won. The rule that the answers always come true stays fully intact.

phrases.english: They are the ones who did not check
whether they would win or be defeated;
but at the last time, when they did check,
they (the Urim VeTummim) agreed,

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵם שֶׁלֹּא בִּיחֲנוּ אִם לְנַצֵּחַ אִם לְהִנָּצֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what was asked: the earlier answers never addressed the outcome
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אורים ותומים told them to fight, which implied victory, and they lost.
steps.terutzMaskana: The early questions never asked about winning. When they did ask, the promised victory came true.

steps.title: The פסוק of פנחס asking about victory
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in שופטים shows that the third question asked whether to keep fighting or stop, and the answer promised victory.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And פנחס son of אלעזר son of אהרן stood before it in those days, saying: Shall I go out again to battle against my brother בנימין, or shall I stop? And ה׳ said: Go up, for tomorrow I will give him into your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to prove the answer it just gave. Only in the last inquiry was the outcome asked about, and the answer promised success.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'or shall I stop' show that this time they were really asking whether they would succeed. The reply 'tomorrow I will give him into your hand' is a clear promise of victory. That promise came true.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק as proof)
פנחס son of אלעזר, the כהן who asked the אורים ותומים

phrases.english: as it is said: "And Pinchas son of Elazar son of Aaron
stood before it in those days, saying:
Shall I yet again go out to battle
against the children of Benjamin my brother,
or shall I cease?
phrases.notes: This shows the question now concerned the outcome.

phrases.english: And God said: Go up,
for tomorrow I will deliver him into your hand."
phrases.notes: שופטים כ:כח

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וּפִנְחָס בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַהֲרֹן עוֹמֵד לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural proof for the answer in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That the final inquiry asked about victory and was answered with a promise of success

steps.title: How did the answer actually appear?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the אורים ותומים physically gave its answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: How was it done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question about how the answer appeared on the חושן. It is setting up the disagreement that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The names of the שבטים were engraved on the stones of the חושן. The question is how those letters turned into a readable answer for the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: How is it done?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the method by which the answer was given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical way the אורים ותומים communicated an answer

steps.title: Letters stand out or letters join together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the letters of the answer stood out. ריש לקיש says the letters joined together to form the words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: the letters stuck out. ריש לקיש says: the letters came together.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question of how it worked, and they disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the needed letters lit up or protruded, and the כהן גדול had to put them in order himself. According to ריש לקיש, the letters themselves moved into the right order, so the words were already formed. Both agree that the answer came through the engraved letters.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who holds the letters protrude
An אמורא who holds the letters join together

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: they protrude.
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול then arranges the letters into words.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: they join together.
phrases.notes: The letters arrange themselves into words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 with two views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: the letters protrude. ריש לקיש: the letters join into words.

steps.title: The letter צ is missing
steps.stepSummary: The names of the שבטים contain no צ, so how could every answer be spelled?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the letter צ is not written in them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that answers were spelled from the letters on the חושן. It points out that one letter is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of the twelve tribal names contains the letter צ. If any answer might need a צ, the stones could not spell it. This problem applies to both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: But the letter tzadi is not written in them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the letter-based mechanism described in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that every answer could be formed from the letters on the חושן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The tribal names lack a צ, so some words could not be formed.

steps.title: The names of the אבות were also written
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק says אברהם, יצחק, and יעקב were also engraved, and יצחק supplies the צ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יצחק said: 'אברהם יצחק ויעקב' was written there too.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the challenge by adding to what was engraved on the חושן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides the twelve tribal names, the names of the אבות were also on the stones. The name יצחק has a צ, so the missing letter is now available.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives this answer
The three אבות, whose names were also engraved

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak said:
"Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob" is written there.
phrases.notes: יצחק contains a צ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק: אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב כְּתִיב שָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the missing-צ challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding information: more words were engraved
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the twelve tribal names were on the חושן, so צ was missing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The names of the אבות were also engraved, and יצחק supplies the צ.

steps.title: The letter ט is still missing
steps.stepSummary: Even with the names of the אבות, there is still no ט.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the letter ט is not written!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. Even after the names of the אבות are added, another letter is still missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither the tribal names nor אברהם, יצחק, and יעקב contain a ט. So the full alphabet is still not available, and some answers could not be spelled.

phrases.english: But the letter tet is not written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up challenge that survives the answer of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the full alphabet was on the חושן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No engraved name, tribal or patriarchal, contains a ט.

steps.title: The words שבטי ישורון were also written
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says 'שבטי ישורון' was also engraved, and שבטי supplies the ט. Now the whole alphabet is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: 'שבטי ישורון' was written there too.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא answers the last challenge by adding one more phrase that was engraved on the חושן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase שבטי ישורון ('the tribes of ישורון') was also on the stones. The word שבטי contains a ט. With this, every letter of the alphabet was available, so any answer could be spelled.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives this answer
The tribes of ישורון, a phrase also engraved on the חושן

steps.whatToRemember: The אורים ותומים answered through the letters on the חושן. Those letters either protruded (רבי יוחנן) or joined into words (ריש לקיש). To make the full alphabet available, the חושן had the twelve tribal names, plus אברהם יצחק ויעקב (for צ), plus שבטי ישורון (for ט).

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
"The tribes of Jeshurun" is written there.
phrases.notes: שבטי contains a ט.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: שִׁבְטֵי יְשׁוּרוּן כְּתִיב שָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the missing-ט challenge of step 14 and completes the alphabet.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding information: another phrase was engraved
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even with the names of the אבות, ט was missing.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבטי ישורון was also engraved, supplying the ט, so the full alphabet was present.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a כהן גדול without רוח הקודש cannot be asked
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a כהן גדול who lacks רוח הקודש and שכינה cannot be asked through the אורים ותומים. The proof is that צדוק got an answer and אביתר did not. This challenges the idea that the letters alone produced the answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: Any כהן who does not speak with רוח הקודש, and on whom the שכינה does not rest, may not be asked through. For צדוק asked and it worked for him, while אביתר asked and it did not work for him. As the פסוק says: 'And אביתר went up until all the people had finished.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with what was just said, that the letters on the breastplate stood out or joined together to spell the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the letters spell the answer by themselves, the כהן's spiritual level should not matter. Yet the ברייתא says a כהן without רוח הקודש cannot be asked at all. It proves this from אביתר, who stopped getting answers. On the other side, if the כהן already has רוח הקודש, why does he need the אורים ותומים at all?

keyTerms.meaning: It worked for him / he got an answer
A כהן גדול in דוד's time who lost the ability to get answers

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not argue that the letters did not light up. The question is only why the כהן's רוח הקודש would matter if the letters already show the answer.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְדַבֵּר בְּרוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: Any priest who does not speak with the Divine Spirit
and [on whom] the Divine Presence [does not] rest
phrases.notes: The word 'not' carries over from the previous phrase.

phrases.english: may not be consulted [through the Urim VeTummim],
for Zadok asked and it worked for him,
Ebiathar [asked] and it did not work for him,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיַּעַל אֶבְיָתָר עַד תּוֹם כׇּל הָעָם וְגוֹ׳״!
phrases.english: as it says: 'And Ebiathar went up until all the people finished, etc.'!
phrases.notes: This is read to mean אביתר was removed from his post because רוח הקודש had left him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the mechanism from step 11, where the letters stood out or joined together, by showing that the כהן's spiritual level was required.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the letters of the breastplate themselves showed the answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the letters give the answer by themselves, רוח הקודש should be unnecessary. If רוח הקודש is present, the אורים ותומים should be unnecessary. The ברייתא requires both.

steps.title: רוח הקודש assisted the letters
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that רוח הקודש helped the אורים ותומים. The two worked together.
steps.simpleTranslation: It [רוח הקודש] was helping along with them [the אורים ותומים].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in one short line: the כהן's רוח הקודש and the letters worked as a team.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters only formed the answer if the כהן was worthy. His רוח הקודש was not strong enough to give the answer without them, so both were needed. This keeps step 11 in place and fits the ברייתא about אביתר.
steps.whatToRemember: An answer from the אורים ותומים needed two things: the letters on the breastplate and a כהן גדול worthy of רוח הקודש.

phrases.english: It [the Divine Spirit] would assist together with them [the Urim VeTummim].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining both elements: the letters and רוח הקודש each play a role.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either the letters alone give the answer, or רוח הקודש alone does.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are needed: רוח הקודש assists, and the letters show the answer.

steps.title: What is the source that only a king may ask?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the אורים ותומים may be asked only for a king. It then asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they may ask only for a king.' From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the משנה's next rule and asks where it comes from. This sets up רבי אבהו's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was how the אורים ותומים works. Now the question is who may ask. The משנה limits this to a king and other national leaders, and the גמרא wants a פסוק for that limit.

keyTerms.meaning: We ask only for a king
From where are these things known?

phrases.english: 'And they may consult only for a king.'
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of how the answer appears and turns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for limiting questions to the king and national leaders.

steps.title: רבי אבהו derives it from the פסוק about אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו cites the פסוק where יהושע stands before אלעזר the כהן to ask through the אורים. Each phrase points to a different leader: 'he' is the king, 'all of Israel with him' is the משוח מלחמה, and 'all the congregation' is the סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The פסוק says, 'And he shall stand before אלעזר the כהן, who shall ask for him by the judgment of the אורים...' 'He' is the king. 'And all the children of Israel with him' is the כהן anointed for war. 'And all the congregation' is the סנהדרין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question with a פסוק and reads three of its phrases as three kinds of leaders who may ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about יהושע, who had the status of a king, so 'he' means a king. All of Israel follows the משוח מלחמה into battle, so 'all the children of Israel with him' refers to him. 'All the congregation' means the סנהדרין, the heads of the nation. Since the פסוק names only leaders, an ordinary person cannot ask.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן anointed to lead the army in war

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'הוא', 'וכל בני ישראל אתו', and 'וכל העדה' come from the end of the same פסוק. They are hidden inside the 'וגו׳' (etc.). They are not from a new פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: Only national leaders may ask the אורים ותומים: the king, the משוח מלחמה, and the סנהדרין.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the אורים ותומים was for national matters, not private questions.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: for the verse states:
'And before Elazar the priest he shall stand,
and he shall ask for him by the judgment of the Urim, etc.'
'He': this is the king,
phrases.notes: It refers to יהושע, who had the status of a king.

phrases.english: 'And all the children of Israel with him':
this is the priest anointed for war,
'And all the congregation': this is the Sanhedrin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: במדבר כ״ז:כ״א: the phrases of the פסוק mean the king, the משוח מלחמה, and the סנהדרין.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק בא לו כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing formula that ends the פרק of בא לו כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, בא לו כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא marks the end of the פרק with the traditional הדרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It formally closes the פרק. The next פרק, יום הכפורים, opens with a new משנה about the five prohibitions of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the end-of-perek formula)
Name of the perek being completed

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ בָּא לוֹ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: We will return to you, 'The High Priest Came'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the perek after the final derivation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The perek ends after setting out how the אורים ותומים works and who may ask through it.

steps.title: The משנה lists the things forbidden on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists five kinds of affliction on יום הכפורים. It then records a מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and חכמים about leniencies for a king, a bride, and a חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On יום הכפורים it is forbidden to eat, drink, wash, anoint, wear leather shoes, or have marital relations. רבי אליעזר says a king and a bride may wash their faces, and a woman who just gave birth may wear shoes. חכמים forbid all of these.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new פרק begins with a משנה that lists everything forbidden on יום הכפורים. It also records a disagreement about special cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list has five categories, often called the five עינויים: eating and drinking, washing, anointing, shoes, and relations. רבי אליעזר lets a king and a bride wash their faces so they look presentable, and lets a חיה wear shoes for her health. חכמים do not make these exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who recently gave birth

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חיה' does NOT mean an animal. It means a woman who has just given birth.
steps.whyThisMatters: The word 'אָסוּר' in the משנה's first line becomes the target of the גמרא's first question in step 23.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Yom Kippur is forbidden
phrases.notes: The opening word 'אסור' is what the גמרא will question.

phrases.english: in eating, in drinking, and in washing
and in anointing, and in wearing a shoe,
and in marital relations.
But the king and the bride may wash their faces,
and a woman after childbirth may wear a shoe,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Sages forbid it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new perek right after the הדרן in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All five עינויים are forbidden on יום הכפורים. רבי אליעזר allows exceptions for a king, a bride, and a חיה, and חכמים forbid them.

steps.title: The משנה gives the amounts for eating and drinking
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets the amount that makes a person חייב: a large date (ככותבת הגסה) for food and a cheekful (מלא לוגמיו) for drink. Foods combine with foods and drinks combine with drinks, but food and drink do not combine with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who eats the size of a large date, counting the date and its pit, or drinks a cheekful, is חייב. All foods add up together toward the date-size, and all drinks add up together toward the cheekful. Food and drink do not add up together.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the exact amounts that make someone liable for eating or drinking on יום הכפורים. It also explains which amounts may be added together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the amount is a large date, not the usual כזית used for other foods. Different foods count together, and different drinks count together. Eating and drinking are measured separately and never combine.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of a large date

steps.confusionAlert: The amount on יום הכפורים is NOT a כזית. It is a large date, because the measure here is about whether a person feels settled after eating.

phrases.english: One who eats the size of a large date,
like it together with its pit,
or one who drinks a cheekful, is liable.
All foods combine toward the date-size,
and all drinks combine toward a cheekful.
One who eats and drinks: they do not combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by giving the amounts for eating and drinking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The amount for food is a large date and for drink is a cheekful. Foods combine with foods and drinks with drinks, but food and drink do not combine.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say only 'forbidden' when the punishment is כרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that the משנה used the soft word 'אסור', since eating on יום הכפורים is punished with כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'forbidden'? But this is punished with כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by challenging the משנה's choice of words in its very first line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אסור' sounds like a plain prohibition. Eating on יום הכפורים is far more severe, since it carries כרת. So the משנה should have used a stronger word, such as 'חייב'.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Forbidden?!
It is punishable by karet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the משנה in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'אסור' in the משנה's opening line
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An act punished with כרת deserves a stronger word than 'forbidden'.

steps.title: The word 'forbidden' is there to cover a half-measure
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילא, and some say רבי ירמיה, answers that 'אסור' teaches that even less than the full amount, a חצי שיעור, is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא said, and some say it was רבי ירמיה: The word is needed only for a half-measure.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the challenge. The word 'אסור' was chosen on purpose to teach about a smaller amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full date-size brings כרת. Eating less than that brings no כרת, but it is still forbidden. The משנה's word 'אסור' covers this smaller case.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than the full amount that brings punishment
And some say (the statement was by someone else)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ila said, and some say Rabbi Yirmeya:
It is needed only for a half-measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the word to a different case (a smaller amount)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אסור' was a weak way to describe the כרת prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אסור' refers to a חצי שיעור, which is forbidden but carries no כרת.

steps.title: What about the view that a half-measure is allowed by Torah law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. It works if a חצי שיעור is forbidden מן התורה, but what about the view that it is permitted מן התורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says a half-measure is forbidden by Torah law. But for the one who says a half-measure is permitted by Torah law, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses on the answer from step 24 and asks how it fits a different opinion. This sets up the next move, which brings in the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a חצי שיעור is permitted מן התורה, it seems the משנה would not call it 'אסור'. So the answer of step 24 seems to work for only one side. Steps 26–28 name the two views and answer this question: even ריש לקיש agrees a חצי שיעור is forbidden מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for the one who says...

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says
a half-measure is forbidden by Torah law,
but for the one who says
a half-measure is permitted by Torah law,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר חֲצִי שִׁיעוּר אָסוּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 24 by testing it against another opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that 'אסור' refers to a חצי שיעור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a חצי שיעור is permitted מן התורה, it seems the משנה could not call it 'אסור', so the answer appears to fit only one view.

steps.title: The dispute about a half-measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the source of the view mentioned in step 25. רבי יוחנן says a חצי שיעור is forbidden מן התורה. ריש לקיש says it is permitted מן התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: about a half-measure, רבי יוחנן said it is forbidden by the Torah, and ריש לקיש said it is permitted by the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is showing where the two views from step 25 come from. It names the people who hold each view, which sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 only said 'some hold one way, some hold the other.' Now we learn it is a famous מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. This lets the גמרא aim its question directly at ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than the full amount that makes a person liable
Permitted by Torah law (though the Rabbis may still forbid it)
As it was stated (introduces a recorded dispute of אמוראים)

steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת is one of the most important background disputes in all of ש"ס. It comes up again and again whenever a small amount of a forbidden food is discussed.

phrases.english: As it was stated: regarding a half-measure,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אָסוּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: it is forbidden by Torah law,

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מוּתָּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: it is permitted by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the two views mentioned in the challenge of step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: a חצי שיעור is forbidden מן התורה. ריש לקיש: a חצי שיעור is permitted מן התורה.

steps.title: The challenge restated against ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The answer of רבי אילא works for רבי יוחנן. But for ריש לקיש, who says a חצי שיעור is permitted מן התורה, why would the משנה say 'אסור'?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי יוחנן. But according to ריש לקיש, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the challenge from step 25, now using the names. For ריש לקיש, the word 'אסור' seems to have no explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a חצי שיעור is permitted מן התורה, then the משנה's word 'אסור' cannot be teaching a Torah prohibition on small amounts. So the answer of רבי אילא seems to fit only רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (a sharp challenge)

phrases.english: This works well according to Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?
phrases.english: but according to Reish Lakish, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אֶלָּא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the names from step 26 to sharpen the challenge of step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילא's explanation (step 24) that 'אסור' teaches a חצי שיעור is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to ריש לקיש a חצי שיעור is permitted מן התורה, so the word 'אסור' cannot point to a Torah prohibition on it.

steps.title: ריש לקיש agrees it is rabbinically forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Even ריש לקיש admits that a חצי שיעור is forbidden מדרבנן. So the משנה's word 'אסור' fits his view as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש agrees that it is forbidden by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. ריש לקיש only said a חצי שיעור is allowed by Torah law, but he agrees the Rabbis forbade it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אסור' does not have to mean a Torah prohibition. For ריש לקיש it means a rabbinic prohibition. So the משנה still teaches that even a small amount is not allowed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ריש לקיש allows eating a חצי שיעור in practice. He only says the Torah does not forbid it. Everyone agrees it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish agrees
that it is forbidden by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the opinion: the prohibition is rabbinic, not absent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought ריש לקיש holds a חצי שיעור is fully permitted, so 'אסור' would not fit his view.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש agrees a חצי שיעור is forbidden מדרבנן, so 'אסור' fits both views.

steps.title: Challenge from the oath not to eat
steps.stepSummary: If ריש לקיש says a חצי שיעור is forbidden מדרבנן, then an oath about a חצי שיעור of forbidden food should not bring a קרבן שבועה. But a משנה teaches that someone who swore not to eat and then ate forbidden foods is liable, and רבי שמעון exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should not be liable for an oath-offering on it. Yet we learned in a משנה: 'An oath that I will not eat,' and he ate נבילות, טריפות, שקצים or רמשים, he is liable. רבי שמעון exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 28 with a new question about oaths. It quotes a משנה from מסכת שבועות as the source of the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath cannot take hold on something that is already forbidden. If a חצי שיעור is already forbidden מדרבנן, it seems an oath on it should not take hold, so there should be no קרבן שבועה. The full force of this question becomes clear once we see, in the next steps, that ריש לקיש himself explains this משנה as talking about a חצי שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering brought for breaking an oath
Yet we learned in a משנה
Animals that died without proper שחיטה, and animals with a fatal defect

phrases.english: If so,
he should not be liable for an oath-offering on it,
yet we learned in a mishnah:
'An oath that I will not eat,'
and he ate carcasses and tereifot,
forbidden creatures and creeping creatures, he is liable.
And Rabbi Shimon exempts him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, לָא נִיחַיַּיב עֲלֵיהּ קׇרְבַּן שְׁבוּעָה, אַלְּמָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 28, that ריש לקיש holds a חצי שיעור is forbidden מדרבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ריש לקיש holds a חצי שיעור is forbidden מדרבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a חצי שיעור is already forbidden, an oath on it should not take hold. Yet the משנה makes the person liable for a קרבן שבועה.

steps.title: Why should the oath take hold at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls its earlier discussion of that משנה. Why is the person liable? He was already sworn at הר סיני not to eat these foods, so a new oath should not take hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: why is he liable? He is already sworn from הר סיני!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in an earlier discussion about the משנה it just quoted. This sets up the two explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath cannot take hold on something the person is already sworn against. Every Jew was 'sworn' at הר סיני not to eat נבילות and the like. So how can his private oath make him liable?

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (recalls an earlier discussion)
Already under oath from Mount Sinai

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
Why is he liable?
He is already sworn from Mount Sinai!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes an earlier challenge on the משנה cited in step 29, as background to the question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the person is liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An oath cannot take hold on foods that are already forbidden by the Torah, which is like an oath from הר סיני.

steps.title: He included permitted foods in the oath
steps.stepSummary: רב, שמואל and רבי יוחנן answer that the משנה is talking about someone whose oath covered permitted foods together with forbidden foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב, שמואל and רבי יוחנן say: the case is where he included permitted things together with forbidden things.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to the question of step 30. Since his oath also covers permitted foods, it takes hold, and it then takes hold on the forbidden foods as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath that takes hold on permitted foods can also take hold on forbidden foods in the same oath, since they are included together. That is why he is liable even for eating נבילות.

phrases.english: Rav, Shmuel and Rabbi Yochanan, who say:
where he includes permitted things
together with forbidden things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oath was only about forbidden foods, so it could not take hold.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath included permitted foods too, so it takes hold on everything.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the oath was about a half-measure
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a different answer. The משנה can only be explained where the person clearly swore about a חצי שיעור, following the חכמים, or where he swore with no detail (the sentence continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: you can only find it where he clearly said a half-measure, according to the חכמים, or where he said it with no detail,
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש begins his own explanation of the משנה. He says it works when the oath was about a חצי שיעור. This passage ends in the middle of his sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ריש לקיש holds a חצי שיעור is not forbidden מן התורה, a person was never sworn about it at הר סיני, so an oath on it can take hold. This is the root of the question in step 29: if a חצי שיעור is forbidden מדרבנן, why does ריש לקיש let the oath take hold? According to the חכמים, a plain oath 'not to eat' only covers a full amount, so he must spell out 'a half-measure'.

keyTerms.meaning: You can only find it (the case) in
According to the view of the חכמים

steps.confusionAlert: The step is not finished. 'או בסתם' continues on the next amud, where we learn which view makes a plain oath cover even a tiny amount.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
you only find it
where he explicitly states a half-measure,
and according to the Rabbis,
or where he swore with no detail,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אִי אַתָּה מוֹצֵא אֶלָּא
